q: Which element is best for the main navigation links of a page?
why: <nav> is a semantic landmark: screen readers can jump straight to it.

q: Which attribute gives an image text for screen readers?
why: alt describes the image for people who can't see it and shows if it fails to load.

q: Which tag creates the most important heading?
why: <h1> is the top-level heading. Use one per page for a clear outline.

q: What is CSS mainly used for?
why: CSS controls presentation: colour, spacing, layout, animation.

q: Which CSS feature lets you reuse a value like a brand colour everywhere?
why: Custom properties (CSS variables) like var(--accent) are the base of design tokens.

q: Which layout system is designed for two-dimensional rows AND columns?
why: Grid handles rows and columns together; Flexbox is one-dimensional.

q: What does 'perspective' do on a parent element?
a: Makes child 3D transforms look like real depth
why: perspective sets the viewing distance so rotateX/rotateY children shrink with depth. It powers the tilt cards on this site.

q: What does 0.1 + 0.2 evaluate to in JavaScript?
why: Numbers are binary floating point. That's why this site stores money as whole-peso integers.

q: Which keyword declares a variable that can't be reassigned?
why: const prevents reassignment (the object it points to can still change).

q: Why use textContent instead of innerHTML for user-provided text?
why: innerHTML parses markup, so '' could run code. textContent treats everything as plain text.

q: Which HTTP status code means 'Not Found'?
why: 404 = the resource doesn't exist. 500 is a server error; 200 is success.

q: Which HTTP method is normally used to CREATE a new resource?
why: POST creates; GET reads; PATCH/PUT update; DELETE removes.

q: Why must a server re-check prices sent by the browser?
a: Users can modify requests, so the client can't be trusted
why: Anyone can edit a request with DevTools or curl. The server must be the source of truth.

q: What does the WCAG AA guideline ask for normal text contrast?
why: 4.5:1 for normal text (3:1 for large text). Check it in the Color Lab.
